chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:

I said to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'A woman sits by the head of the patient while she is menstruating, at the time of death.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm in her looking after him. But when they fear for him and that time is near, let her move away from him and from his proximity, for the Angels are harmed by that.'

key_terms.تُمَرِّضَهُ: She looks after him / nurses him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a menstruating woman caring for a dying patient in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of a menstruating woman nursing a patient, distinguishing between general care and the critical moment of death (al-hadl). It introduces a specific spiritual sensitivity, noting that Angels are affected by her state, which necessitates her moving away from the immediate vicinity as death approaches. This ruling highlights the intersection of physical hygiene and spiritual purity in Shia jurisprudence during the transition of the soul.
